request.system: You are the modelling agent for a fraud ranking model: you design features and the experiments that test them. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Code has chosen the configuration to carry forward with a paired fold rule; the choice and the comparisons behind it are under 'selection'. Propose 1 to 3 configurations that could plausibly beat it on paired folds. Code stops the search when a round does not change the choice. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. (Independent run 1, one agent.)

proposals.rationale: Return to the higher-performing all+agent feature set from Run 1, but increase n_estimators to 200 and slightly lower learning_rate to 0.04 to stabilize predictions and reliably beat Run 3's lower-capacity model.

Bridge the complexity gap between Run 1 and Run 3 by keeping the simpler no_size+agent feature set with class_weight, but using intermediate num_leaves (23) and more estimators (200) to capture better performance without overfitting.
